name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,403

clue.text: Takes off for journey aboard ship

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
SS is steamship, the usual abbreviation for a ship

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a voyage by boarding a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' reads like departing, but here it means removing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to remove clothing, which is what someone does when they take garments off.

clue.text: Blade used in argument over filling of roulade

indicators.note: the filling of something is what lies at its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: a spat is a petty quarrel
the three central letters of the word roulade

explanation.surface: A knife is wielded in a kitchen row over what goes inside a rolled sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat, broad-bladed kitchen tool used for spreading and lifting food.

clue.text: Assortment of goods originally stolen from country house

indicators.note: what something was originally is how it began, so only the opening letter is kept
something stolen from a place is taken away, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: the opening letter of goods
a grange is a country house with farm buildings

explanation.surface: A burglar makes off with a mix of items from a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: A grange is a British country house, often with farm buildings attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of products is a varied selection of them, the same sense as an assortment.

clue.text: Popular trick involving Russia's foremost snack

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept
to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: pop is short for popular
a con is a swindle or trick
the opening letter of Russia

explanation.surface: A well-loved stunt involving the leading Russian is followed by something to nibble.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is a familiar light snack of heated, puffed maize kernels eaten at the cinema.

clue.text: Gooey Greek starters served in retro purple tableware

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so the opening letters of each word are kept
food served in a dish sits inside it, so one piece goes within another
retro means backward-looking, so the colour word is read backwards

blocks.note: the initial letters of the two words
puce is a brownish-purple colour

explanation.surface: A meze of sticky Greek appetisers is presented on old-fashioned purple crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like the food course, but it picks out first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg cup is a small holder for a boiled egg, one item of crockery set on a breakfast table.

clue.text: Setter leaving cold building with masonry walls is blue!

indicators.note: when the setter leaves, that letter departs from the word that follows
the walls of a thing are its outside edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
an igloo is a dome of snow blocks
the first and last letters of masonry

explanation.surface: A setter quits a chilly stone house and feels down.
explanation.walkthrough: IGLOO loses its I, the setter, and the edges of masonry follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of sad or depressed matches gloomy, meaning low in spirits.

clue.text: Start to carry weapon to protect dog mistreated in noisy performance

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept
something mistreated is knocked about, so its letters are jumbled
to protect something is to surround it, so the weapon goes around the other piece

blocks.note: the first letter of carry
a lance is a long spear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes up arms to defend an ill-treated dog in a loud scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dance is performed in wooden-soled shoes that clatter loudly on the floor, so it is a noisy show.

clue.text: Section of book containing research forecast

indicators.note: one thing containing another holds it inside, so the second piece goes within the first

blocks.note: a page is a leaf of a book
res is the abbreviation for research

explanation.surface: A chapter of a book holds study results that make a prediction.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or predict, the verb sense of forecast.

clue.text: Hotel croupier misdealt to famous Belgian

indicators.note: cards misdealt are handed out wrongly, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A casino dealer at a hotel deals badly to a well-known Belgian guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotel' looks like the H of the phonetic alphabet, but the whole word joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's moustachioed detective is the best-known Belgian character in fiction, a fair example.

clue.text: Sailor close to mountain lake ...

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
the final letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A seaman approaches a lake high in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small lake lying in a hollow among mountains, especially in northern England.

clue.text: ... Calls about more unusual bodily secretions

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are set out of order
about means around, so the first piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: phones as a verb means calls
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the mountain lake, someone telephones about strange discharges from the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheromones are chemicals released by animals that affect others' behaviour, a kind of secretion from the body.

clue.text: 10 entertained by duet playing close to disco's DJ

indicators.note: musicians playing rearrange themselves, so these letters are shuffled into a new order
a guest entertained by hosts is held among them, so the number goes inside
the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
X is ten in Roman numerals, not the entry numbered 10
the final letter of disco

explanation.surface: A disc jockey is amused by a pair of performers at the end of a disco night.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' tempts a solver to use the answer at 10-across, but it is simply the Roman numeral. DJ here means dinner jacket, not disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: DJ is a British abbreviation for dinner jacket, and a tuxedo is the American name for that formal evening jacket.

clue.text: Entertainer and press taken in by scam

indicators.note: something taken in by another is absorbed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the press is the news media
a con is a swindle

explanation.surface: A performer and journalists are both fooled by a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken in' reads as deceived, but it is the signal for putting one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer who entertains audiences by making them laugh.

clue.text: Push graduate to meet new so-called composer

indicators.note: so-called means named this way, pointing to a word as it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
N is the abbreviation for new
the German-born composer of Messiah, said out loud

explanation.surface: A graduate is shoved forward to be introduced to a newly famous musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To manhandle someone is to shove or move them roughly by force, so push is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Dates carved into Polish memorial

indicators.note: something carved is cut up and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged
going into something means ending up inside it, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
to hone is to sharpen or polish

explanation.surface: Years of birth and death are chiselled into a smooth stone monument.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Polish suggests the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to make smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the inscribed stone set at a grave to commemorate the person buried there.

clue.text: Stake poked into malignant effigy

indicators.note: something poked into the following words is buried inside them, running across the gap

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A pin is driven into a voodoo doll by someone wishing harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stake' paints a spike stuck in the doll, but it is the gambling sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the bet each player puts into the pot before the deal, a stake.

clue.text: Cold and uncooked crop

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
raw food is not cooked

explanation.surface: A harvest is chilly and not yet prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' suggests a harvest, but it is the pouch in a bird's throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A craw is the crop of a bird or insect, the pouch in the gullet where food is stored before digestion.

clue.text: Cigar found by biblical king scratching backside in bed

indicators.note: scratching off the backside removes the tail, so the king's name loses its final letter
lying in something means being inside it, so the shortened name sits within the bed

blocks.note: Herod was king of Judaea in the gospels
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A cigar is discovered beside an ancient monarch who lies scratching his rear in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square, open at each end.

clue.text: A pass key is in circulation around Delaware's last illicit bar

indicators.note: the last of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
something in circulation moves around, so these letters are mixed into a new order
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go either side of the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the final letter of Delaware

explanation.surface: Copies of a door key are passed around a secret drinking den in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A speakeasy was a bar selling alcohol illegally during American Prohibition, so an unlicensed drinking place.

clue.text: Sportsman attending hospital allowed to get drug

blocks.note: to be at an event is to attend it
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
let means allowed
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An injured player in hospital is permitted some medication.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is someone who competes in sport, especially track and field events.

clue.text: Curse about outer layer of Terylene garment

indicators.note: the outer layer of a word is its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept
about means around, so the curse word wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: to swear is to curse
the first and last letters of Terylene

explanation.surface: Someone swears about the synthetic fabric in a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Terylene is a British brand of polyester fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted top worn on the upper body, one kind of garment.

clue.text: Anglican chorister's tie?

blocks.note: the end of the first word joins the start of the second

explanation.surface: A church choirboy's neckwear is asked about.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no indicator: the question mark warns that the answer sits across the first two words. 'Tie' looks like neckwear but is the verb for fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor something is to fix or secure it firmly in place, as one would tie it down.

clue.text: Collapse after endless torture by one in European capital

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: hell is torment
to sink is to collapse or subside
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone breaks down after relentless torment by a person in a European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the collapse piece behind the shortened torture word.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital city of Finland, so it is one of Europe's capitals.

clue.text: Hot meal prepared by Troy's prince

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been made up, so these letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
taken as written
t is the abbreviation for troy, the system of weights for precious metals

explanation.surface: A warm dinner is cooked by a prince of ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troy's prince' suggests Paris or Hector; Troy is in fact troy weight, and the prince is Danish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is Shakespeare's Prince of Denmark, so the title character is a prince.

clue.text: Slight uprising over length of factories

indicators.note: in a down clue a word rising up is read from bottom to top, so backwards
the reversed word is placed over and around the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: slim means slight or slender
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A minor revolt breaks out over the length of the working day in the works.
explanation.definitionFit: Mills are buildings where goods are manufactured, such as cotton mills, so factories.

clue.text: Working with Old Master, returned to church somewhere in Italy to produce black and white picture

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so these first pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
OM is the abbreviation for Old Master
CH is the abbreviation for church
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: An Old Master painter goes back to an Italian church to create a picture without colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A monochrome is an image in shades of a single colour, typically a photograph in black and white.

clue.text: Tenor leaving coffee behind

indicators.note: when the tenor leaves, that letter departs from the coffee word

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A singer walks out, abandoning his cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like the place the coffee is left, but it is the definition: running behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being late means being behind schedule, arriving after the expected time.

clue.text: Other people accepting central elements of informed speculation

indicators.note: the central elements of a word are its middle letters, which alone are kept
accepting something means taking it in, so the people word holds the other piece

blocks.note: they refers to other people
the two middle letters of informed

explanation.surface: Others take on board the heart of an educated guess.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a supposition or idea put forward to explain something, which is speculation.

clue.text: Fragments of screen found in ceremonial vessel

indicators.note: fragments are broken pieces, so these letters are scattered and put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pieces of a broken screen turn up inside a church vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A censer is a container in which incense is burned during religious ceremonies.
